destination.title: Moduli stabilization, control and consequences
destination.question: How do specified compactification dynamics fix or leave moduli mobile, when are the resulting effective descriptions consistent, and what vacuum, particle-physics and cosmological consequences follow?
destination.summary: A broad organizing proposal with an IIB Kähler-stabilization concentration, distinct flux and nonperturbative settings, and explicit neighboring questions about runaways and geometric limits. Numerical proximity alone does not justify a common physical premise.

systems: Source-specified type IIB geometric and non-geometric compactifications
Type IIA orientifolds and their stated M-theory duals
Heterotic stabilization and hidden-sector orbifold condensation settings
targets: Modulus potentials, stabilization and remaining flat directions
Sector separation, superpotential consistency and approximation control
Vacuum energy, local stability, distributions and searches
Supersymmetry breaking, soft terms and cosmological dynamics
regimes: Distinct classical, perturbative and nonperturbative constructions
Large-radius, exponentially large-volume and moderately large-volume settings kept separate
Static vacua, partial stabilization and time-dependent boundary cases
assumptions: Only source-specific assumptions apply; membership supplies no universal flux, hierarchy, uplift or control premise
conventions: Positive stationary points, stable minima and globally realized compactifications are different targets
Source-scoped identities preserve the original unit statements
includes: Conditional constructions, consistency tests and qualitative toy models
Alternative mechanisms represented by the outside probes
excludes: Treating numerical membership as scientific equivalence
Treating K3 tensor limits or enhancement singularities as evidence of Kähler stabilization
Universal claims of controlled de Sitter vacua or completed stabilization

sources.title: Jumping Through Loops: On Soft Terms from Large Volume Compactifications

evidence.text: Does the conjectured KK correction spoil stabilization and the gaugino hierarchy in the explicit two-modulus large-volume model?

sources.title: Type IIA/M-theory Moduli fixing in a Class of Orientifold Models

evidence.text: How does a complex constant superpotential contribution enable moduli stabilization in a class of Type IIA orientifolds and their M-theory duals, and how do consistency restrictions and vacuum distributions depend on the chosen Kähler potential?

sources.title: String Loop Moduli Stabilisation and Cosmology in IIB Flux Compactifications

evidence.text: Under what geometric and perturbative conditions can type IIB LARGE Volume Scenarios stabilize Kähler moduli, and what inflationary and finite-temperature cosmology follows?

sources.title: Sequestering in String Compactifications

evidence.text: Does sequestering by geometric separation or strong warping survive nonperturbative stabilization of Kähler moduli, and what soft terms follow in KKLT and Large Volume Scenario compactifications?

sources.title: Building an explicit de Sitter

evidence.text: Can a global type IIB construction realize Kähler uplifting with explicit branes and fluxes, geometric moduli stabilized in metastable de Sitter, and sufficiently large condensing gauge groups for volume control?

sources.title: Explicit de Sitter Flux Vacua for Global String Models with Chiral Matter

evidence.text: Can explicit flux stabilization of the dilaton and complex structure be combined with Kähler stabilization admitting de Sitter minima in a globally consistent type IIB compactification with chiral matter?

sources.title: Aspects of moduli stabilization in type IIB string theory

evidence.text: How do KKLT and LVS stabilize type IIB moduli, and what consequences follow for supersymmetry breaking, low-energy phenomenology, inflation, destabilization and moduli backreaction?

sources.title: A new class of de Sitter vacua in String Theory Compactifications

evidence.text: Can the complex-structure sector remain stable after quantum corrections in large-volume type IIB vacua whose volume is only moderately large, especially when the number of moduli exceeds O(100)? Can stability arise without making this sector much heavier than the gravitino?

sources.title: The Swampland Conjecture and F-term Axion Monodromy Inflation

evidence.text: Can KKLT stabilization retain a heavy Kähler modulus while a quantized open-string coupling generates a sufficiently light inflaton and a large backreaction threshold?

sources.title: Racing through the swampland: de Sitter uplift vs weak gravity

evidence.text: Two confining gauge sectors coupled to one Kähler modulus can provide competing exponentials that separate the stabilized modulus mass from the vacuum energy. The same competition produces axion interference and motivates checking both the assumed superpotential and the resulting field-distance scales.

sources.title: Racing through the swampland: de Sitter uplift vs weak gravity

evidence.text: A stabilized type-IIB Kähler modulus must remain locally stable when positive supersymmetry-breaking energy is added. The baseline model combines a logarithmic Kähler potential, a flux constant, a single condensate exponential, and an anti-D3 energy proportional to the inverse square of the volume modulus.

sources.title: Swampland Variations on a Theme by KKLT

evidence.text: Can the Kähler modulus be stabilized below the already exponentially light conifold modulus while the latter generates the small superpotential required by KKLT?

sources.title: The $F$-term Problem and other Challenges of Stringy Quintessence

evidence.text: The classical no-scale sector supplies flat Kähler directions on which small corrections can generate quintessence. The same sector also controls the gravitino mass and ordinary modulus-mediated soft masses.

sources.title: Rigid nongeometric orientifolds and the swampland

evidence.text: The rigid quotient supplies an explicit setting for comparing Bianchi formulations and testing positive stationary potentials. Its retained sector has three Kähler moduli and no complex-structure moduli.

sources.title: A systematic approach to Kähler moduli stabilisation

evidence.text: Can type IIB Kähler-modulus stabilization be performed directly in 2-cycle variables, avoiding difficult inversion to 4-cycle coordinates and enabling systematic searches beyond familiar KKLT and LVS geometries?

sources.title: Moduli Stabilisation and the Statistics of SUSY Breaking in the Landscape

evidence.text: How does including Kähler-moduli stabilization change the statistical distributions of the gravitino mass and visible-sector soft terms in the type IIB flux landscape?

sources.title: Dilaton stabilization in KKLT revisited

evidence.text: When does flux stabilization make the dilaton sufficiently heavy to avoid a saddle generated by mixing with the nonperturbatively stabilized Kähler modulus, and what constraints does this impose on complex-structure stabilization and NS three-form flux?

sources.title: IIB String Theory and Sequestered Inflation

evidence.text: Can steep type-IIB flux potentials stabilize heavy moduli while leaving supersymmetric Minkowski flat directions that can subsequently support plateau inflation?

sources.title: Thraxions: towards full string models

evidence.text: How do nonzero thraxion VEVs affect internal geometry, and does their extreme mass suppression survive Kähler moduli stabilization? Which global CY orientifolds can support these sectors?

sources.title: Uplifts in the penumbra: features of the moduli potential away from infinite-distance boundaries

evidence.text: Can subleading contributions retained between the interior of complex-structure moduli space and its strict infinite-distance limits produce positive local minima and long axion valleys useful for de Sitter uplifting or inflation?

sources.title: Coexisting flux string vacua from numerical Kähler moduli stabilisation

evidence.text: Can a modular numerical framework recover different Kähler-stabilization mechanisms across many geometries and identify distinct local vacua coexisting at identical effective flux parameters, enabling studies of transitions within one potential?

sources.title: Moduli evolution in the presence of flux compactifications

evidence.text: Can a cosmological background fluid prevent overshoot and stabilize both components of a complex volume modulus in flux-inspired potentials, and how does the stabilization basin depend on initial conditions and the fluid equation of state?

sources.title: The Scaling of the no scale potential and de Sitter model building

evidence.text: Can positive local minima of the no-scale potential in complex-structure and axiodilaton directions replace the antibrane volume source in KKLT-like (A)dS model building?

sources.title: Building a better racetrack

evidence.text: Which concrete KKLT-type compactifications have sufficient nonperturbative contributions to stabilize all Kähler moduli, and can flux stabilization supply the required small, nonzero W0?

sources.title: Moduli stabilization in the heterotic/IIB discretuum

evidence.text: How do nonperturbative superpotentials change supersymmetric flux Hodge types, and can heterotic moduli stabilization avoid both non-Kähler geometry and negative gauge kinetic functions?

sources.title: Effective potentials for light moduli

evidence.text: Does integrating out flux-stabilized heavy moduli before adding nonperturbative superpotential terms give a consistent light-modulus potential, and can the omitted contributions permit positive F-term minima without uplifting?

sources.title: KKLT type models with moduli-mixing superpotential

evidence.text: How does moduli mixing in nonperturbative superpotentials change KKLT stabilization, parameter tuning, modulus/anomaly mediation, and cosmological stability when one modulus is already heavy?

sources.title: Gaugino and Scalar Masses in the Landscape

evidence.text: Does nonperturbative Kähler-modulus stabilisation preserve a gravitino–gaugino mass hierarchy across the IIB landscape, and can large-volume models yield approximately flavour-universal scalar masses?

sources.title: Jumping Through Loops: On Soft Terms from Large Volume Compactifications

evidence.text: The proposed diagnostic compares a candidate DBI-induced tension with a corresponding Chern–Simons charge term under BPS assumptions. Applying it to the listed flux–curvature terms remains heuristic.

sources.title: Type IIA/M-theory Moduli fixing in a Class of Orientifold Models

evidence.text: Construct the four-dimensional N = 1 F-term potential V = e^K(g^{I J̄}D_IW D_J̄W̄ − 3|W|²). Use homogeneity identities, eliminate the axion-dependent W1 combination, and solve supersymmetry equations and polynomial branches of ∂_I V = 0.

sources.title: String Loop Moduli Stabilisation and Cosmology in IIB Flux Compactifications

evidence.text: Uses low-energy loop scaling and the Coleman–Weinberg potential to motivate corrections and cancellations; expresses the one-loop scalar potential through the tree-level Kähler metric and conjectured Kähler-potential correction.

sources.title: Sequestering in String Compactifications

evidence.text: Reviews supergravity separability using f=−3MPl² exp[−K/(3MPl²)] and additive visible/hidden superpotentials. The weaker extended no-scale criterion is K̃_ab̄=exp[K̂/(3MPl²)]κ_ab̄ with F^m∂mκ_ab̄=0; eliminating moduli-mediated A terms additionally requires F^m∂mYabc=0.

sources.title: Building an explicit de Sitter

evidence.text: Flux search starts from rational moduli and an approximate prepotential constant, solving W0=DSW0=DU1W0=DU2W0=0 linearly for integer fluxes subject to the tadpole bound. Supersymmetry equations are then solved with instanton corrections and the exact constant; Kähler stabilization is numerical.

sources.title: Explicit de Sitter Flux Vacua for Global String Models with Chiral Matter

evidence.text: Toric Mori cones, divisor intersections and mirror symmetry determine the polynomial prepotential. Picard–Fuchs equations and the mirror map determine instanton corrections and periods in an integral symplectic frame. Calculations use PALP, Sage and Instanton.

sources.title: Systematics of String Loop Corrections in Type IIB Calabi-Yau Flux Compactifications

evidence.text: Which combinations of quantum corrections and additional sources can stabilize Kähler moduli while preserving a controlled large-volume expansion? The appendix compares mechanisms by their competing potential terms, flux-superpotential magnitude, topology, and gauge-sector assumptions.

sources.title: Axion Stabilization in Type IIB Flux Compactifications

evidence.text: Can B2 and C2 axions in type IIB orientifolds with h1,1− ≠ 0 be stabilized within extensions of KKLT/LVS, and how do their corrections affect volume stabilization?

sources.title: Probability of vacuum stability in type IIB multi-Kähler moduli models

evidence.text: How often is the Kähler-moduli Hessian positive definite at extrema of concrete large-volume Type IIB models, and how does this conditional probability differ between supersymmetric KKLT-like stabilization and nonsupersymmetric LVS stabilization?

sources.title: Towards the core of the cosmological constant problem

evidence.text: Can a proposed Type IIB self-tuning mechanism cancel the cosmological constant despite nonzero moduli and brane vacuum energies, using a negative-potential KKLT minimum as the present background?

sources.title: A Geometrical Upper Bound on the Inflaton Range

evidence.text: Does partial moduli stabilization remove every infinite-distance direction, or can the remaining flat Kähler sector still support arbitrarily large scalar excursions? The paper asks this within LVS, using the internal Kähler cone and the induced kinetic metric.

sources.title: Runaway in the Landscape

evidence.text: This construction removes Kähler moduli so that a type IIB flux superpotential can involve every surviving geometric modulus and the axio-dilaton. It supplies a setting in which flux stabilization can be studied without adding the usual Kähler-modulus superpotential terms.

sources.title: Non-perturbative stabilization of two Kähler moduli in type-IIB/F theory and the inflaton potential

evidence.text: Does extending nonperturbative stabilization from one to two Kähler moduli, together with perturbative Kähler corrections and D-term uplift, produce slow-roll plateau potentials and viable inflationary parameters?

sources.title: On Gauge Mediated SUSY Breaking and Moduli Stabilization

evidence.text: Can gauge-mediated SUSY breaking dominate in a type IIB model with stabilized moduli and tuned vacuum energy, and can the SUSY-breaking matter sector consistently be treated independently of nonperturbatively stabilized Kähler moduli?

sources.title: Duality invariant gaugino condensation and one loop corrected Kahler potentials in string theory

evidence.text: How do moduli-dependent string thresholds and one-loop corrections to the Kähler potential modify duality-invariant hidden-sector gaugino condensation, scalar potentials, moduli determination, and dilaton stabilization, with or without massive matter?

sources.title: Nonrenormalization of flux superpotentials in string theory

evidence.text: Can holomorphy and perturbatively surviving symmetries establish nonrenormalization of the Type IIB flux superpotential despite its explicit tree-level dilaton dependence, thereby supporting controlled moduli-stabilization arguments?

sources.title: Systematics of String Loop Corrections in Type IIB Calabi-Yau Flux Compactifications

evidence.text: Which cycle can support the nonperturbative contribution used to stabilize a small modulus inside a much larger compactification? The source selects a rigid blow-up cycle resolving a point-like singularity and distinguishes this requirement from the unfluxed instanton eligibility statement.

sources.title: On D-brane dynamics and moduli stabilization

evidence.text: How do forces among pinned fractional branes, antibranes and orientifold planes modify Kähler-modulus potentials, and under what conditional circumstances do they assist or obstruct stabilization? The stated aim is qualitative illustration through a toy model, rather than a realistic stabilized compactification.

sources.title: Quintessence and the Swampland: The Parametrically Controlled Regime of Moduli Space

evidence.text: The setting isolates dilaton and Kähler runaways while treating complex structure as a fixed spectator sector. Large but finite moduli are used to discuss effective supergravity without asserting that the strict infinite-distance boundary itself is phenomenologically viable.

sources.title: String Landscape and the Standard Model of Particle Physics

evidence.text: How can fluxes stabilize compactification parameters when the displayed superpotential omits Kähler moduli?

sources.title: Leaving the Swampland: Non-geometric fluxes and the Distance Conjecture

evidence.text: The STU model tests how a non-geometric interaction changes a Kähler runaway while the complex structure and axio-dilaton remain approximately frozen. The added superpotential term is linear in T and cubic in U.

sources.title: Large Field Ranges from Aligned and Misaligned Winding

evidence.text: Can the small divisor supporting a nonperturbative effect be isolated from complex-structure dynamics? The proposed test sends the surrounding boundary to infinity at fixed blow-up volume and assumes that the remaining local geometry has no complex-structure deformations.

sources.title: Moduli Stabilization in Type IIB Orientifolds (II)

evidence.text: Which resolved toroidal type IIB orientifolds permit closed-string moduli stabilization in the large-radius KKLT framework, and what obstructs a controlled uplift when complex-structure moduli are absent?

sources.title: Racing through the swampland: de Sitter uplift vs weak gravity

evidence.text: What is the actual holomorphic superpotential when two confining gauge sectors share a perturbatively massless dynamical coupling modulus? Determining its branch structure could decide whether the long-period interference assumed in racetrack stabilization survives.

sources.title: The de Sitter swampland conjecture and supersymmetric AdS vacua

evidence.text: Can flux choices isolate one complex Kähler modulus so that a large-radius potential and an interior vacuum can be compared within the same effective theory?

sources.title: Logarithmic loop corrections, moduli stabilisation and de Sitter vacua in string theory

evidence.text: The unfixed fields are Kähler volumes in a type IIB flux compactification. The studied configuration uses three orthogonal D7 stacks so that D-terms can fix two volume ratios while a logarithmically corrected F-term potential controls the total volume.

sources.title: Preference for a Vanishingly Small Cosmological Constant in Supersymmetric Vacua in a Type IIB String Theory Model

evidence.text: Does scanning flux parameters in a specified KKLT-type supersymmetric IIB model statistically favor negative cosmological constants close to zero, and how do the characteristic magnitude and probability of a positive real-modulus Hessian change with the number of complex-structure moduli?

sources.title: On Moduli Stabilization Scheme in Type IIB Flux Compactifications

evidence.text: When can two-stage stabilization of heavy dilaton/complex-structure fields and a light Kähler modulus reproduce the one-stage treatment through a holomorphic effective superpotential, particularly of KKLT or Villadoro–Zwirner form?

sources.title: Systematics of String Loop Corrections in Type IIB Calabi-Yau Flux Compactifications

evidence.text: How do quantum corrections lift the tree-level Kähler-modulus flat directions of type IIB flux compactifications? The effective description separates flux-sensitive axio-dilaton and complex-structure fields from cycle-volume moduli whose perturbative dynamics arise through the Kähler potential.

sources.title: String Gases and the Swampland

evidence.text: Do non-toroidal compactifications and shape-modulus potentials admit analogous stabilization and relative-gradient bounds, and what replaces the toroidal coefficient 1/√p?

sources.title: Racetrack Potentials and the de Sitter Swampland Conjectures

evidence.text: Does an un-uplifted Type IIB moduli potential admit a positive stationary point after complex-structure fields, the dilaton and the Kähler field are all varied?

sources.title: Purely nonperturbative AdS vacua and the swampland

evidence.text: Can flux stabilization yield exactly W0 = 0 before Kähler stabilization? The reviewed symmetry-restricted IIB/F-theory example provides a candidate starting point.

sources.title: Runaway Quintessence, Out of the Swampland

evidence.text: The setting isolates one light complex modulus after other string moduli have been stabilized in a supersymmetric Minkowski vacuum. Its Kähler geometry determines how a geometric saxion coordinate becomes a canonically normalized cosmological scalar.

sources.title: Purely nonperturbative AdS vacua and the swampland

evidence.text: Competing nonperturbative exponentials stabilize one Kähler modulus after flux-sector stabilization. The principal construction uses three terms and W0 = 0.

sources.title: The $F$-term Problem and other Challenges of Stringy Quintessence

evidence.text: Anisotropy is used to lower the lightest KK cutoff at a given volume and thereby suppress the radiative mass of a Kähler shape modulus. Two large dimensions provide the preferred fixed-order-one-W0 scaling in the source's estimate.

sources.title: Moduli stabilization in toroidal type IIB orientifolds

evidence.text: Can the first KKLT stage stabilize every modulus of resolved toroidal type IIB orientifolds, including twisted Kähler moduli, and which divisor geometries and orientifold choices permit nonperturbative superpotentials?

sources.title: Moduli stabilisation and inflation in type IIB/F-theory

evidence.text: Can perturbative corrections in a type IIB/F-theory effective model stabilize Kähler moduli at positive vacuum energy, and can an additional Fayet–Iliopoulos contribution permit volume-modulus slow-roll inflation?

sources.title: Quantum Log-Corrections to Swampland Conjectures

evidence.text: Does a nonperturbative stabilization mechanism necessarily produce the same leading logarithmic modulus enhancement as KKLT?

sources.title: de Sitter vacua in the string landscape

evidence.text: What does stabilization mean when some internal moduli evolve? Constant base volume in case (3.2) still allows changing geometric parameters, motivating a prescription more general than time-independent moduli values.
